title: A whole-invoice fee with no labor or parts dollars goes to one side
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have two active staff members at the test location with their "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A and sales rep B.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Make sure the test location's Shop Supplies Charge is 0% and nothing else is invoiced at the test location today.
  • Have a first work order for that customer with only a whole-invoice fee of $25.00 (no labor or parts dollars), Labor set to sales rep A and Parts set to sales rep B, and invoice it today.
  • Have a second work order for that customer with only a whole-invoice fee of $25.00 (no labor or parts dollars), Labor reading "Unassigned" and Parts set to sales rep B, and invoice it today.
  • Have a third work order for that customer with only a whole-invoice fee of $25.00 (no labor or parts dollars) and both sides reading "Unassigned", and invoice it today.
  • Open Reports > Sales By Representative in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide, with the date range set to today and Show Unassigned on.
custom_steps:
1. Expand sales rep A.
  2. Expand sales rep B.
  3. Expand "Unassigned".
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The first work order's $25.00 is credited to sales rep A, the labor representative.

Step 2:

  • The second work order's $25.00 is credited to sales rep B, the parts representative, because its labor side has no representative.

Step 3:

  • The third work order's $25.00 is credited to Unassigned.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R8: “A whole-invoice amount on an invoice with no labor and no parts dollars goes to the labor representative. If the labor side is empty and the parts side is not, it goes to the parts representative. If both are empty, it is Unassigned. A side is empty when it has no representative.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 23: “23. (a) The labor side has no sales representative.”
